placements.why: This envelope's content is a calibration record — instrument, frequency, and verification against a named reference standard — and no existing strata category holds organizational content of this kind. Future calibration envelopes (other instruments, other reference cycles) will keep feeding this category, making it a legible top-level organizational tier rather than a one-off leaf.
placements.title: Instrument calibration as an organizational category of record
placements.frame: What instrument, parameter, and reference standard ground this calibration claim, and does the verification method meet the org's evidentiary bar?

placements.title: Calibration confidence is grounded in deferral to a fixed external reference
placements.frame: What external standard is invoked to ratify this calibration, and does the claim hold across the full operating range or only at a single checked point?
placements.why: All three expressions state the same directional theme: the Kestrelwood spectrograph's 88.4 MHz calibration is trustworthy because it was checked against the June reference plates and holds across the full observing band. This is a subject future calibration envelopes will keep feeding (new instruments, new reference cycles, new verification episodes) rather than a one-time fact — src-2 and src-3 are the labelled-field decomposition of src-1's prose claim, all pulling toward the same theme of reference-grounded verification. No existing leaf covers this (graph is empty), so it mints fresh under the newly-minted Calibration strata.
